stem:
Nandini looks at the diagram. Straight lines $p$ and $q$ lie on the same flat page and meet at point $R$.

Which claim correctly names the lines and the angle structure at $R$?

options.text: Lines $p$ and $q$ are intersecting, and their meeting at $R$ forms four angles.
Lines $p$ and $q$ can meet at two different points on the page if they are drawn longer.
Call $p$ and $q$ parallel, because they lie on the same flat page.
The four angles at $R$ force lines $p$ and $q$ to be parallel.

teacher.key_rationale: On one flat page, two straight lines that meet at a single point are intersecting, and that meeting forms four angles.
teacher.figure_note: rewrite: intersecting lines p and q at R with four angle marks
